author: Federico Hatoum
body:
I had similar issues when working through getting both cameras set up. There are a few things I would try:
1. I know you double-checked everything, but check again. More than once I had an errant space or semicolon make its way into the scripts which made them not work correctly.
2. Try lowering the resolution of your webcam to 640x480. It just might be set to something that's making it choke.
3. Try getting the webcam to work by itself, without the PI cam.
4. See if you can successfully switch the PI cam to a different port.
5. Reboot between changes.

Hope one of those helps!

author: Federico Hatoum
body:
No, we can't. However, video for linux (v4l), which is the process/system that the cameras run on, does give them permanent IDs.
Problem is that the octopi scripts don't know how to read those values. This is why we set up those simlinks in 99-USB using device and vendor IDs.

author: Federico Hatoum
body:
I share your frustration with video for linux (v4l) -- which is the system that manages the cameras. I've experienced these kinds of issues as well.

One possible solution is using "static" paths to cameras that v4l creates. When you attach a v4l device to a PI, v4l creates entries under /dev/v4l/by-path. I tried using those paths, as they are unchanging, even if you move a camera to a different USB port. Unfortunately, the octopi scripts that manage camera connections don't work in the non-standard /dev/videoX paths.

author: Federico Hatoum
body:
Thank you and congrats on getting the cameras working. :D

To make the usb cam the main webcam, either change the "Webcam" Stream URL under Settings: Features: Webcam & Timelapse, or install the MultiCam Octoprint plugin. (https://plugins.octoprint.org/plugins/multicam/)

You can configure which camera is used for timelapses under the same config tab, but you can only make timelapses from one camera at a time.

body:
The very simplest way is to disconnect the Raspberry PI Camera from your RPI, and removing the RaspiCam entry from Octoprint's Multicam plugin and restart your PI.

The scripts you created using the tutorial will still run, but since the RaspiCam is no longer connected, it will get ignored.

author: Alex Balcanquall

Don't set the FPS flag for the sub cam, remove that option all together.
It disables mjpeg streaming from the camera and crucifies frame rate. TBH i have no clue why every article says to use it when they should say remove it. https://github.com/jacksonliam/mjpg-streamer/blob/master/mjpg-streamer-experimental/plugins/input_uvc/README.md

author: Federico Hatoum
body:
Not sure what to tell you, but I just tested my octopi install by setting the frame rate on the USB camera to various values and removing it completely. mjpeg was not disabled with any setting.

Also, the -f flag doesn't "crucify" frame rate -- it lowers it from a maximum, in order to lower CPU usage -- as it's designed to do.

That said, CPU usage was only slightly lower when I set the framerate to 10 fps compared to not having the flag on at all.

body:
I've had that experience too: changes only take effect after multiple reboots. I don't know why that's the case.
Regarding the MultiCam plugin...
First, confirm that you can view output from both cameras in a browser by visiting the stream URLs for your PI Cam and your USB camera. Then, you add the stream URLs to your MultiCam configuration. Here are my URL strings. If you don't have a local domain set up, you can use your PI's IP address:
http://octopi.local:8080/?action=stream
http://octopi.local:8081/?action=stream

author: Federico Hatoum
body:
What doesn't work, specifically? The PI cam, the USB cam?
Have you tried different troubleshooting steps? For example, do you see the symbolic link for your USB camera in the /dev directory? What happens when you visit the streaming webpage for your cameras? (ex: http://octopi.local:8081/?action=stream).
You need to methodically step through the tutorial, making sure that each step was successful before moving on to the next.
By the way, reinstalling octopi is not necessary. Once it's installed, reinstalling just makes you lose all your progress.

author: HermannSW
body:
Thanks very much for these good instructions.
My borescope USB2.0 camera has no serialNumber, as stated here under troubleshooting removing serial entry worked.
Then webcamd2 service did not start (init_VideoIn failed), as stated above I powered my Pi3A+ down, switched USB cables in mini USB hub (Pi3A+ has only 1 USB interface by default) and powered again.
After that borescope camera works on port 8081 !!
Until now I used gstreamer pipeline on my OctoPi (https://forum.prusaprinters.org/forum/user-mods-octoprint-enclosures-nozzles/simple-nozzle-camera-borescope-holder-for-prusa-mini/#post-582439) and viewed it with vlc (tcp://octopi3ap:8887) on Linux, or vlc app on smartphone (the borescope camera provides detailed nozzle view).
So now both cameras are served with mjpg-streamer.
I hoped to have either both camera views shown in OctoPrint webgui, or have a toggle there to switch between both cameras ...

body: Congratulations Hermann! I'm glad to hear that you got your borescope camera working. To view both of my cameras in the OctoPi UI, I use the MultiCam plugin.

body: Hi Max. What are the ports you have assigned to both cameras? In the instructions, I set camera 1 to port 8080 and camera 2 to port 8081. The output above shows an issue binding to port 8080. If you accidentally have both cameras bound to port 8080, then the second one won't work for sure.
